nodes.summary: For a continuous velocity over a finite alphabet, `ω(s, t) = ∫_s^t ∑_j |vʲ(u)| du`, the `ℓ¹` length of the path between `s` and `t`, is a control function on every set of times (continuous, nonnegative for `s ≤ t`, zero on the diagonal and additive, hence superadditive).
nodes.title: The length of a path is a control

nodes.summary: A control on a set of times $J$ is a function $\omega(s, t)$ of $s \le t$ in $J$ that is continuous, nonnegative, zero on the diagonal and superadditive: The $p$-th power of the $p$-variation of a path over $[s, t]$ is the basic example; the length $\int_s^t |\dot X_u|\,du$ of a path of bounded variation is another. Lyons calls $\omega$ regular when it is continuous near the diagonal and zero on it; the Lean…

nodes.summary: Let $p \ge 1$. There is $\beta_0 > 0$ such that for every $\beta \ge \beta_0$, every control $\omega$ on an interval $J$, and every multiplicative functional $X$ of degree $\lfloor p \rfloor$ whose levels satisfy the extension of $X$ (multiplicative in every degree, of finite $p$-variation, agreeing with $X$ up to level $\lfloor p \rfloor$; unique by the existence and uniqueness part) satisfies the same inequality…
nodes.title: Lyons's extension theorem: the factorial estimate

nodes.summary: For a continuous velocity over a finite alphabet, the signature satisfies Lyons's estimate `‖Sⁱ_{s,t}‖ ≤ ω(s, t)^{i/p} / (β (i/p)!)` with `p = 1`, `β = 1` and `ω` the length of the path, in every degree (T. Lyons, *Differential equations driven by rough signals*, Rev. Mat. Iberoam. 14 (1998), inequalities (2.20)–(2.21)).
nodes.title: The signature of a path of bounded variation is controlled by its length, with `p = 1`

nodes.summary: The levels `1 ≤ i ≤ n` of `X` satisfy `‖Xⁱ_{s,t}‖ ≤ ω(s, t)^{i/p} / (β Γ(i/p + 1))` for `s ≤ t` in `J`, where `Γ(i/p + 1) = (i/p)!` (T. Lyons, *Differential equations driven by rough signals*, Rev. Mat. Iberoam. 14 (1998), Lemma 2.1.1 and inequality (2.20)).
nodes.title: `p`-variation controlled by `ω` (Lyons)

nodes.summary: For a path whose velocity is interval integrable on every interval, `(s, t) ↦ S(X)_{s,t}` is a multiplicative functional of every degree, on every set of times: this is Chen's identity (T. Lyons, Rev. Mat. Iberoam. 14 (1998), §2.1, where multiplicative functionals are introduced as the abstraction of Chen's identity for iterated integrals).
nodes.title: The signature is a multiplicative functional

It abstracts Chen's identity: the signature of a path is one, in every…
nodes.title: Multiplicative functional of degree n (Lyons)

Then for every $i$, where $\omega(s,t)$ is the $\ell^1$ length of the path between $s$ and $t$. So the levels of the signature decay factorially; this is the case $p = 1$, $\beta = 1$ of Lyons's control $\omega^{i/p}/(\beta\,(i/p)!)$, and the reason the signature series of a linear controlled equation converges.

can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
